## 1B.9 Research Note: Narendra Modi in 2024

**Assessment:** The 2024 record is **moderately positive** for precaution and institutional handling of catastrophic-risk-adjacent domains, but the evidence is mostly **indirect**. The clearest support is India’s public tightening of **dual-use export controls** and AERB’s visible safety oversight for civilian nuclear projects. I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence of a dedicated, transparent Modi-led framework for **AI, cyber, or bio-risk governance** specifically.

### Accepted claims

- **Title:** [DGFT to discuss trade regime of dual-use goods, software and technology on Jan 30](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2000179)  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / DGFT, Ministry of Commerce & Industry  
  **Date:** 28 Jan 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2000179  
  **Claim-level summary:** The government convened a strategic trade-controls conference with MEA and other agencies, focused on SCOMET compliance and dual-use controls, with UN 1540 and MTCR participation. This is strong evidence of **precautionary institutional handling** of dual-use risk and some transparency about the control framework.  
  **Question IDs:** 1B.9, 1B.6, 1B.7

- **Title:** [DGFT updates the SCOMET List with recent policy changes and updates in the multilateral export control regimes](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2051331&lang=2&reg=48)  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / DGFT, Ministry of Commerce & Industry  
  **Date:** 3 Sep 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2051331&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim-level summary:** India updated its strategic trade-control list, aligned it with multilateral regimes, and stated that it regulates dual-use, nuclear-related, and military items using licensing, enforcement, and risk assessment mechanisms. This supports a finding of **precaution over improvisation** in dual-use domains.  
  **Question IDs:** 1B.9, 1B.6, 1B.7

- **Title:** [AERB Grants Permission for First Approach to Criticality of 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2039099&lang=2&reg=48)  
  **Publisher:** Atomic Energy Regulatory Board / PIB  
  **Date:** 30 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2039099&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim-level summary:** AERB approved first criticality only after phased core loading, multi-tier safety review, site inspection, and resident-site-observer oversight. This is direct evidence of **precaution, institutional scrutiny, and accident-prevention discipline** in a catastrophic-risk domain.  
  **Question IDs:** 1B.9, 1B.3, 1B.7

- **Title:** [AERB Grants Permission for First Approach to Criticality of Rajasthan Atomic Power Project - Unit 7](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2053554&lang=1&reg=3)  
  **Publisher:** Atomic Energy Regulatory Board / PIB  
  **Date:** 10 Sep 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2053554&lang=1&reg=3  
  **Claim-level summary:** AERB said approval followed comprehensive safety assessments and continuing oversight by its resident observer team. This is more evidence that the state used **technical review and monitoring** rather than opaque political decisionmaking.  
  **Question IDs:** 1B.9, 1B.3, 1B.7

- **Title:** [US National Security Advisor calls on Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2025954)  
  **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office / PIB  
  **Date:** 17 Jun 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2025954  
  **Claim-level summary:** The meeting centered on iCET progress in semiconductors, AI, telecom, defence, critical minerals, and space. This is indirect but relevant evidence that Modi’s government treated advanced-technology risk through **institutional channels** rather than purely ad hoc political handling.  
  **Question IDs:** 1B.9, 1B.7

- **Title:** [Ministry of Home Affairs: Year End Review 2024](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2088945&lang=2&reg=48)  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Home Affairs  
  **Date:** 31 Dec 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2088945&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim-level summary:** The review highlights security apparatus upgrades, including DAE/DRDO-origin explosive detectors being handed to IB and a high-level review of MAC operations. This supports a cautious reading that the government was willing to deploy **technical tools and institutional processes** in security work.  
  **Question IDs:** 1B.9, 1B.7

### Countervailing / weaker evidence

- **Title:** [Shri Amit Shah reassumes charge as Union Home Minister in North Block, New Delhi today](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2024244&lang=2&reg=48)  
  **Publisher:** Ministry of Home Affairs / PIB  
  **Date:** 11 Jun 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2024244&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim-level summary:** The security portfolio remained centered on Modi and Amit Shah, with strong “zero tolerance” political framing. This is only a **weak negative signal**: it suggests centralized political control, but it does not show that experts were actually displaced in a catastrophic-risk decision.  
  **Question IDs:** 1B.9, 1B.7

### Search gap

- I found **no strong 2024 evidence** of a Modi-led precaution/transparency framework specifically for **cyber, AI, or biological risk**.
- I found **no direct evidence** of public red-teaming, independent oversight, or open catastrophic-risk reporting for those domains.
- So the best-supported conclusion is: **precaution is visible in dual-use and nuclear-safety administration, but evidence is thin for AI/cyber/bio-specific transparency.**
